Whole-body, organ, and cellular transport
A typical strategy for delivering fat-soluble vitamins to targeted organs and cells is transport by lymphatic chylomicrons. The lipid
bilayer structure allows uncharged hydrophobic molecules, such as lipids, to pass through cell membranes by diffusion driven by
differences in the concentration gradient. In addition, it is now apparent that for speciﬁc lipids, such as cholesterol and fat-soluble
